To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interaction between stray electrostatic field and a charged test mass can cause force noise, that this noise can be measured, and that it can be nullified.
the electrostatic field inside an enclosure with a conducting wall is not uniform and that it can be measured with two independent techniques.
the stray electrostatic fields inside a conducting enclosure are not a significant noise source in the LISA mission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between a charged test mass and a stray electrostatic field.
the interaction of stray electrostatic fields with a charged free-fall test mass.
the development of a new technique to measure stray electrostatic fields in a conducting enclosure and its application to the LISA mission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, with a properly designed experiment, it is possible to achieve a force noise below the LISA requirements.
the electrostatic noise is not a limiting factor in the LISA Pathfinder mission.
the stray field problem is solved, at least for the LISA mission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an experimental technique that can measure the electrostatic forces acting on charged test masses with an accuracy that is sufficient for future gravitational wave experiments.
, for the first time, the stray electrostatic fields have been characterized in detail and controlled to the required level for a successful LISA mission.
, with our techniques, it is possible to measure and null the electrostatic forces acting on charged test masses with a precision of 0.5  fm/s2/Hz1/2 for frequencies above 1 mHz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stray fields are not a limiting factor for the LISA mission.
stray electrostatic fields can be controlled to a level that is well below the sensitivity of the LISA gravitational reference sensor, which will allow LISA to achieve its sensitivity goal.
, with the right experimental setup and electrostatic model, it is possible to accurately measure the stray electrostatic fields that interact with a charge in a conducting enclosure.
